engines.name: Unity (Mono)

signatures.basis: convention (game nested one folder down, seen in a real library)

routes.name: BepInEx plugin (Mono)
routes.status: maintained; stable releases exist for Unity Mono on Windows, macOS and Linux
routes.notes: Use the x86 build for 32-bit games, x64 for 64-bit; macOS supports 64-bit only. Under Proton use the Windows build with WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp.dll=n,b" %command%.

routes.name: MelonLoader mod (Mono)
routes.notes: Windows, Linux (native, Wine, Proton) and macOS per its docs. Proton launch option WINEDLLOVERRIDES="version=n,b" %command%.

routes.name: Edit assets (AssetRipper / UnityPy / UABEA)
routes.notes: Extract, change and repack assets without code.

engines.data_only: Config files via BepInEx/config; asset extraction and repack with AssetRipper or UnityPy.
pitfalls: 32-bit vs 64-bit loader build must match the game
Online games with anti-cheat reject modified files

engines.name: Unity (IL2CPP)

routes.name: MelonLoader mod (Il2Cpp)
routes.notes: Needs the .NET 6 Desktop Runtime. Under Proton install it with "protontricks <appid> dotnetdesktop6" and prefer a clean prefix.

routes.name: BepInEx IL2CPP
routes.status: only via Bleeding Edge builds; docs and README disagree (build dates UNVERIFIED)
routes.notes: README says only Unity Mono has stable releases; IL2CPP is Windows and Linux, not macOS.

engines.data_only: Asset extraction and repack with AssetRipper or UnityPy.
pitfalls: Cpp2IL has only pre-release builds; Il2CppDumper is stale
IL2CPP loader support is less stable than Mono

engines.name: Unreal Engine 4/5

signatures.basis: convention (UE4SS install docs name this folder)
convention (IoStore containers are documented by Epic)

routes.name: UE4SS scripting mods
routes.status: maintained (v4.0.0); native Linux builds unsupported, no Proton guidance in its docs
routes.notes: Installs into {game}/GameName/Binaries/Win64 as a dwmapi.dll proxy; the top-level exe is a launcher wrapper. Expect per-game fixes.

routes.name: Browse and repack assets (FModel / repak / UAssetGUI)
routes.notes: Pak files may be AES-encrypted or signed (Epic project settings); IoStore (.utoc/.ucas) is a different container.

engines.data_only: Replace or add .pak contents with repak after unpacking; encrypted paks need the AES key.
pitfalls: Easy Anti-Cheat blocks modified files in protected multiplayer
Encrypted or signed paks cannot be edited without the key

engines.name: Godot

signatures.basis: convention: a godot-named library (for example godotsteam) beside the exe; a pack embedded in the exe leaves no .pck file

routes.name: Patch pack (.pck / .zip) loaded by the game
routes.notes: Works only if the game loads extra packs; check with GDRE Tools first.

routes.name: Inspect or recover the project (GDRE Tools)
routes.notes: Godot 2, 3 and 4; encrypted PCKs need the key.

engines.data_only: Patch PCK or ZIP resource packs.
pitfalls: A pack can be embedded in the exe (no .pck file); the Godot 3 vs 4 pack-format mapping is UNVERIFIED

engines.name: Ren'Py

routes.name: Edit scripts (unrpa + unrpyc, or add .rpy files)
routes.notes: unrpa extracts .rpa archives; unrpyc decompiles .rpyc (it does not extract archives). Ren'Py reads loose .rpy files placed in game/.

engines.data_only: Loose .rpy/.rpyc files and replacement assets in game/.
pitfalls: unrpa has not had a release since 2019

engines.name: GameMaker

routes.name: UndertaleModTool (edit data.win)
routes.status: maintained (0.9.2.0); GUI Windows only, CLI on Windows/Ubuntu/macOS
routes.notes: No official GUI on Linux/macOS: use the CLI, a WIP cross-platform port, or Wine.

routes.name: Unpack app.asar, edit JavaScript, repack

pitfalls: Modifying executables is blocked by most anti-cheat

anticheat.name: Easy Anti-Cheat
anticheat.meaning: Epic says its integrity tool uses a signed catalog of file hashes: modified cataloged files can block you from protected multiplayer sessions, while offline, solo and unprotected modes still run.

anticheat.name: BattlEye
anticheat.meaning: BattlEye's FAQ says it generally bans only for actual cheats or components built to bypass it; overlays and tools like ReShade are generally supported unless the developer says otherwise (blocked in some games), and some programs can get you kicked.

hubs.name: Nexus Mods
hubs.rules: Prohibits uploads that include copyrighted game files or images without permission from the owner; crediting is no substitute. AI policy: disclosure is mandatory for anything made with generative AI (tiers AI-Generated Content, AI Media, AI Assisted); enforced from 2027-01-02 after a 60-day grace period.

hubs.name: Thunderstore
hubs.rules: Do not distribute game files like Assembly-CSharp.dll without permission. AI-generated assets or code should use the AI Generated category where it exists (not enforced for READMEs or icons); untested or non-functional AI mods are spam. A package is a zip with icon.png (256x256), README.md and manifest.json at the root.

hubs.name: Steam Workshop
hubs.rules: Valve may remove Workshop contributions for any reason (Subscriber Agreement 6.B); app-specific terms can add rules. Steam's AI disclosure survey applies to games on Steam, not Workshop items. A Workshop-specific AI rule: UNVERIFIED.

hubs.name: mod.io
hubs.rules: Uploads grant mod.io and the game admin a content licence and you warrant the content does not infringe others' rights; the Acceptable Use Policy applies. No AI clause found in the terms (Acceptable Use Policy not read).

expiries.what: Nexus Mods begins enforcing its AI-content disclosure rules after the 60-day grace period

notes: signatures marked "convention" are file names widely used but not confirmed on a primary page in our research; detection only suggests an engine, the user confirms. Routes marked UNVERIFIED must be checked against the engine's own documentation.
